composite_aspect_frame.conjunction:
In a composite chart a conjunction is a fused function of the relationship itself.

The two principles do not negotiate here, they operate as one thing the pair does - and because this is the relationship's chart rather than either person's, neither party owns it. Whichever of them appears to be carrying it is carrying it on behalf of the bond, which is why the roles can swap without the pattern changing.
composite_aspect_frame.opposition:
In a composite chart an opposition is an axis the relationship has to hold open.

Both ends are the bond's, not one person's each - though the pair will almost always distribute them, with one partner voicing one end and the other the opposite, and each convinced the problem is the other. The work is recognising the split as the relationship's own rather than a difference between two people.
composite_aspect_frame.square:
In a composite chart a square is the friction the relationship runs on.

Two of the bond's own functions want incompatible things, so the tension keeps generating events rather than resolving. This is the recurring argument the pair cannot talk its way out of, because it is structural: it is what the relationship is made of, and the useful question is what it is being used to build.
composite_aspect_frame.trine:
In a composite chart a trine is something the relationship does well without trying.

Two functions of the bond agree, and the ease is real. It is also unexamined - nothing here asks the pair to develop, so a relationship carried mostly by trines is comfortable and tends not to grow. The gift is genuine and it will not announce itself; the couple often cannot say what they are good at.
composite_aspect_frame.sextile:
In a composite chart a sextile is a capacity the relationship has to choose to use.

Two functions cooperate readily, but only when the pair acts on them. Unlike a trine it does not run by itself, and unlike a square it does not force the issue - so a sextile quietly lapses in a relationship that never picks it up, and rewards one that does.
composite_aspect_frame.quincunx:
In a composite chart a quincunx is a mismatch the relationship cannot reconcile, only manage.

The two placements share no element, mode or polarity and traditionally cannot see one another at all, so the adjustment is continual and never finished. It rarely produces open conflict and reliably produces the sense that something in the bond is slightly out of phase with itself.
composite_aspect_frame.semisextile:
In a composite chart a semisextile is a persistent small awkwardness.

Adjacent functions of the bond with nothing in common, held at a tight orb. Not a difficulty so much as a mild recurring friction, and worth reading only where it lands on something that already matters elsewhere in the chart.
composite_aspect_frame.semisquare:
In a composite chart a semisquare is low-grade pressure about practical things.

Half a square and it behaves like one at reduced volume: a recurring irritation about arrangements rather than a confrontation about principles. It accumulates rather than erupts, which is what makes it easy to leave unaddressed for years.
composite_aspect_frame.sesquiquadrate:
In a composite chart a sesquiquadrate is pressure that surfaces after the fact.

The square's other material relative, and it tends to appear once a situation is already in motion. The tension is real and its timing is inconvenient, which is most of why the pair struggles to name what is wrong.
composite_aspect_frame.quintile:
In a composite chart a quintile is a knack that belongs to the pair.

Kepler's aspect of talent: a specific thing this relationship can make or do that neither person manages alone. It causes no trouble and therefore goes unnoticed, which is precisely the argument for looking for it.
composite_aspect_frame.sesquiquintile:
In a composite chart a sesquiquintile is an unconventional facility.

The quintile's further harmonic - an odd, inventive capacity in the bond that will not fit the usual categories. Faint, and distinctly its own thing wherever it does show up.
